hook: A company can buy thousands of AI licenses while its most useful AI work stays unofficial.
readerPromise: Understand what counts as adoption and why visibility, permission and competence can move at different speeds.
protectedRevelations: Detailed adoption prescriptions and the later failed-expectation cases
visualPlan: What becomes visible: Set an unused company license beside a worker quietly finishing a real task. Reveal two short labels, Tried and Relied on, beside the worker's actual work.

From trial to practice: Compare a license receipt, a trial result and a changed routine on one work surface. Let a colleague approach the worker and look at the useful result before reaching for the tool.

The permission gap: Show a finished AI-assisted document on the desk while its author hesitates to mention how it was made. Place the polished document beside an unanswered reviewer question, without a success mark.
Look beneath the noise: Return to the worker considering which task to change next. Keep the visible trial result beside the quieter repeated work, inviting comparison.

cueChanges.nextVisualChange: Contrast a conspicuous public failure with a quiet working document; avoid charts implying measured hidden success.
Reduce the early-adopter demonstration to one worker and one colleague; connect the encounter to accepted practice.
Keep the review table and responsibility document; use a pause before the colleague responds.
Retain the learning exercise as an open question, then replace its old concluding labels with the adoption ladder reading cue.

sentenceIntentions.text: A company can buy thousands of AI licenses while its most useful AI work stays unofficial.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Contrast purchased licenses with useful unofficial work
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize that corporate purchase figures may miss actual dependence

sentenceIntentions.text: AI Adoption Beyond the Slop follows adoption as growing dependence, far beyond trying a tool.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: State the book-specific adoption ladder in the opening
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Understand that repeated dependence matters beyond first trials

sentenceIntentions.text: A purchased license, a clever experiment, and a changed working practice tell very different stories.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Differentiate purchase, trial and working change
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Question what an adoption statistic actually measures

sentenceIntentions.text: The book follows the first users, and the people who help others feel comfortable trying.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Introduce early users and social legitimacy
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Wonder how unfamiliar practices become ordinary

sentenceIntentions.text: It asks why someone might rely on AI privately while avoiding the subject with colleagues.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Expose private use beside public silence
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Recognize the tension between usefulness and professional reputation

sentenceIntentions.text: It also examines what happens when polished output arrives faster than professional judgment develops.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect output abundance with developing judgment
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Feel concern about expertise behind polished work

sentenceIntentions.text: These tensions matter to anyone deciding where AI belongs in their own work.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Connect adoption distinctions with one's own workplace
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Consider which stage their team has actually reached

sentenceIntentions.text: Start with its stages of adoption, and ask what the loudest examples leave out.
sentenceIntentions.purpose: Offer the source's adoption ladder as a starting point
sentenceIntentions.viewerResponse: Want to compare visible examples with deeper dependence

distinctiveContribution: Adoption is a ladder of dependence and social acceptance, so highly visible trials can coexist with hidden consequential use.
